newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican turns nose up at smoked salmon story.
newsitem.headline: Vatican turns nose up at smoked salmon story.

text.p: The Vatican on Monday denied a British newspaper report that Pope John Paul had a liking for Scottish smoked salmon but not for paying the British company that supplied him with it.
In a rare response to a newspaper article, the Vatican issued a statement saying "neither the papal kitchen nor the Holy Father has anything to do with this story".
The Sunday Telegraph newspaper had reported that the family firm Hebridean Seafoods had dropped the Pontiff as a customer because it was fed up with being paid late.
"Getting paid from the Vatican proved as much a miracle as feeding the 5,000," it quoted chairman John Mackenzie as saying.

The paper reported that until recently 200 kilos of salmon, worth about $4,000, was shipped to the Vatican every two weeks. It said the Pope liked the fish because it came from unpolluted waters in the Outer Hebrides off the west coast of Scotland.

The Vatican confirmed it had received smoked salmon from the firm through an Italian importer until July, but said it had cancelled the orders "because of differences over the quality of the product". All the bills had been paid on time, it said.
